body:
## Ask

Bake a **fully autonomous billing and feasibility engine** into the project, derived from the six-materials calculus (paper: *The mechanics of the governance dilemma*). Before any run, the agent is told — plainly, in numbers:

1. **What this run will cost.**
2. **How long it will take.**
3. **How close the system is to long-term stable peak performance**, per coordinate.
4. **Exactly what to adjust**, at this moment, to converge back toward peak.
5. **Whether the job can complete at all** — through the entire pipeline, not just the next step.

## The state vector

Eighteen coordinates: six raw materials x three properties.

| Material | measured from |
|---|---|
| Network | reachability probes, latency and loss to each required endpoint |
| Hardware | memory, free pages, paging pressure, thermal and CPU headroom |
| Software | tool versions against pins, runner health, config drift |
| Agent | model/human presence, load, historical success rate |
| Information | required inputs present and fresh (specs, docs, credential validity) |
| Agency | permissions actually held: merge rights, token scopes, ruleset bypass, credit balance |

Each carries **availability** (present now), **stability** (variance over time), and **reliability** (correct when used). `vibey-gh fit` already measures the hardware-availability and software-availability coordinates; this generalises it to all eighteen.

## Feasibility across the whole pipeline

The verdict must cover every stage, because a run that dies at stage seven wasted stages one through six:

install -> interview -> feature branch -> develop -> develop deployment -> develop validation -> main -> main deployment -> main validation

Each stage declares its requirement vector; the run is feasible only if the state dominates that requirement at every stage it must pass. **Agency shortfalls are the common killer and must be reported first** — a run that cannot merge is infeasible however healthy the hardware, which this project demonstrated repeatedly tonight.

## The report

    vibey-gh estimate --operation "promote 1.65.0"

      feasible: NO - blocked at stage 'main' (agency: merge rights absent)
      cost:     $0.00 local lane (paid lane at zero credit - agency shortfall)
      duration: 14m 20s projected for stages install..develop-validation
      distance from peak:
        network      0.81  stable
        hardware     0.62  free memory 8.8%, below the 20% setpoint
        software     1.00  pins current
        agent        0.94  local reviewer available, reliability 0.31 on nuanced calls
        information  1.00
        agency       0.20  no merge permission; paid credit exhausted
      first repair (steepest descent): restore agency - grant merge rights or fund the paid lane
      second:                          hardware - free 3 GB or reduce concurrency to 8

## Acceptance

- Every number traceable to a measurement, never a default; unmeasurable coordinates report *unknown* and lower the confidence rather than being invented (doctrine 10).
- Feasibility verdicts proven against real runs: a job called infeasible must actually fail at the named stage, and one called feasible must complete.
- Cost accounting covers both lanes — paid API spend and local generation-seconds — because sovereignty means the local lane's cost is also real.
- The repair ranking is the gradient, not a heuristic list, and is shown to reduce time-to-peak on a real recovery.
- Fails loudly at the floor per doctrine 10: an impossible job says so immediately, naming the coordinate that makes it impossible.
- Zero new runtime dependencies.

Related: the six-materials paper section, #263 and #264 (the fit calculus this generalises), #261 (the ledger where state history belongs), vibey#114 (storage tiers), doctrine 10's hardware-decomposition clarification.

Made-With: Made with ❤️ by [Vibey](https://adammatthewsteinberger.github.io/vibey/), Developed by [Adam Matthew Steinberger](https://vibewithadam.matthewsteinberger.com/) ([@adammatthewsteinberger](https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/)).

Likely files: vibey-gh/estimate.py, vibey-gh/fit.py, vibey-gh/report.py

## Triage — 2026-09-17 (`develop` @ f2467910, v0.8.0)

**Status: NOT STARTED** · size **XL** · confidence high

**The ask, as read:** Generalise `vibey-gh fit` from two coordinates to the full 18 (six materials x availability/stability/reliability), add per-stage requirement vectors across install→…→main-validation, and ship `vibey-gh estimate --operation` reporting cost (paid and local lanes), duration, per-coordinate distance from peak, a gradient-ranked repair list, and a whole-pipeline feasibility verdict with agency shortfalls reported first.

### What already ships
- Hardware-availability coordinate, measured honestly (cgroup-aware on Linux, vm_stat/sysctl on macOS, unreadable ≠ zero)
- Software-availability coordinate for the local model runner
- Duration projection: τ fitted from real observations plus a superlinear queueing wait, refitted in a bounded rolling window
- ADMIT/DEFER/FLOOR verdict with the arithmetic in the reason, and a loud floor that names why (satisfies the doctrine-10 acceptance clause for those two coordinates)
- A wired CLI (`vibey-gh fit`) and a journalled control loop with projections and measurements kept strictly separate
- Elsewhere in the monorepo: agent availability/reliability and credit-balance signals already measured and persisted (EngineHealthRecord, `vibey doctor`)

### Evidence in the tree
- /Users/adam/git/vibey/src/vibey_tools/gh/docs/paper.md:268-271 — the paper itself states the position: 'The fit calculus deployed in this system is the two-coordinate projection of this space — hardware availability against software availability'. 2 of 18 coordinates, by the author's own account
- /Users/adam/git/vibey/src/vibey_tools/gh/docs/paper.md:212-266 — the six-materials table, the 18-coordinate state vector x, the dilemma vector d = x* − x, feasible(o) ⟺ x ⪰ r_o, T(o), C(o), and the −∇_d T repair gradient exist as MATHEMATICS IN A PAPER only
- /Users/adam/git/vibey/src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/fit.py:128-147 — `Machine` (total/free/swap + a `readable` flag distinguishing 'unmeasurable' from 'zero'): hardware availability, measured
- /Users/adam/git/vibey/src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/fit.py:464-486 — `sample_model` reads the model from the local runner's /api/ps and returns None rather than assuming: software availability, measured
- /Users/adam/git/vibey/src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/fit.py:490-523 (estimate_from), :526-545 (saturating_wait), :548-554 (headroom_gb), :557-653 (decide) — duration projection and ADMIT/DEFER/FLOOR with a loud floor. This satisfies ask (2) partially and the 'fails loudly at the floor' acceptance clause for the two coordinates it covers
- /Users/adam/git/vibey/src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/cli.py:1193-1211 (parser) and :599-644 (`_fit`) — genuinely wired production entry point `vibey-gh fit`, not dead code; documented at /Users/adam/git/vibey/src/vibey_tools/gh/docs/cli.md
- …and 6 more

### What is actually left
- Add the 16 missing coordinates: network availability/stability/reliability (reachability, latency, loss probes per required endpoint), hardware stability+reliability (thermal, paging pressure, wear), software stability+reliability (versions vs pins, config drift, runner health), agent (presence, load, historical success rate), information (required inputs present and fresh — specs, docs, credential validity), agency (merge rights, token scopes, ruleset bypass, credit balance)
- Add the stability and reliability PROPERTIES generally — today every measurement is a point-in-time availability reading with no variance term and no correctness term
- Model x* and emit per-coordinate distance-from-peak, with `unknown` for unmeasurable coordinates lowering confidence rather than being defaulted (explicit acceptance criterion; the `Machine.readable` flag is the pattern to generalise)
- Declare a requirement vector r_o per pipeline stage (install, interview, feature branch, develop, develop deployment, develop validation, main, main deployment, main validation) and evaluate x ⪰ r_o at every stage, not just the next one
- Report agency shortfalls first in the verdict ordering, per the issue
- Implement cost: price the paid lane (dollars) and the local lane (generation-seconds) into one C(o); today neither reaches fit
- Implement the repair ranking as the actual gradient −∇_d T rather than a heuristic list, and demonstrate it reduces time-to-peak on a real recovery
- Ship `vibey-gh estimate --operation "..."` with the report layout in the issue body, and document it in docs/cli.md
- …and 13 more

### Blockers
- Agency measurement needs live GitHub API reads (merge rights, token scopes, ruleset bypass) — vibey_gh doctor is currently deliberately offline/credential-free, so this changes that module's contract
- 'Proven against real runs' is an empirical acceptance bar that cannot be met by unit tests alone; it needs a harness that records predicted-vs-actual stage failures

> ⚠️ **Verdict corrected by the verifier.** The verdict overstates completion by crediting the issue's own declared starting point as progress. The issue body states verbatim: '`vibey-gh fit` already measures the hardware-availability and software-availability coordinates; this generalises it to all eighteen.' Every artifact the auditor lists as shipped (Machine at /Users/adam/git/vibey/src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/fit.py:128-147, sample_model at :465-487, estimate_from/saturating_wait/headroom_gb at :490-554, decide at :557-653, FitLoop at fitloop.py:100-271, the wired `vibey-gh fit` at cli.py:599-644 and :1193-1212) is that pre-existing baseline. Git proves it: fit.py and fitloop.py entered the repo in ce6c2cce (2026-09-15, 'chore: import vibey-gh into src/vibey_tools/gh (history preserved)'), and the ONLY subsequent change to either file is 14f44fc0 (PR #176, 2026-09-16), whose full commit body I read -- a Linux /proc/meminfo and cgroup memory-reading bug fix citing doctrine 10, never #134. No commit in #181-#207 touches this ask.

All five numbered asks are unimplemented. (1) Cost: grep for cost|usd|price|dollar over fit.py and fitloop.py yields exactly one hit, fitloop.py:147, the English word 'cost' in a docstring; no cost model exists for either lane. (2) Duration: fit.py:490-554 projects ONE local inference's wall time against ONE deadline, not the nine-stage install->interview->...->main-validation pipeline the issue's report specifies. (3) Distance from peak: no x*, no d = x* - x, no per-coordinate score; `grep -rni "requirement.vector|distance from peak|dilemma_vector"` over all of src/ hits only paper.md:212,248. (4) Gradient repair: fitloop.py:253-271 recommendation() is a two-branch hard-coded string (FLOOR reason, else 'grow paging space') -- exactly the heuristic the acceptance criterion rejects. (5) Pipeline feasibility: `grep -rn "feasib"` across src/vibey/ and src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/ returns ZERO hits outside paper.md; no stage model exists.

Two auditor claims are category errors. The ADMIT/DEFER/FLOOR verdict at fit.py:557-653 does not satisfy the doctrine-10 acceptance clause ('naming the coordinate that makes it impossible'): it can name memory or an unreadable model and cannot name the other sixteen coordinates because it has never measured them. And even the two coordinates it covers are incomplete against the issue's own table -- hardware is defined as 'memory, free pages, paging pressure, thermal and CPU headroom', while grep for thermal|loadavg|cpu over vibey_gh/ returns nothing.

Agency, the coordinate the issue calls 'the common killer' and orders reported first, has no measurement anywhere: `grep -rni "agency"` over src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/ and src/vibey/ returns nothing. The auditor's own negatives check out (no `estimate` in the full add_parser inventory at cli.py:931-1290 including the four looped parsers at :960/:1007/:1261/:1285; doctor.py:19 'no network, no credentials, no execution'; EngineHealthRecord at dto.py:167-185 and `vibey doctor` at cli/main.py:1030+ are a different tenant with no path into fit) -- but the auditor listed the last of those under 'shipped parts' while conceding it feeds nothing. With zero of five asks and zero of six acceptance criteria met, and the only cited code being the baseline the issue names, the honest verdict is not-started.

**Notes:** This is the only one of the four with real shipped substance — but the substance is 2/18 of the state vector plus duration. Cost (the 'billing' half of the title), whole-pipeline feasibility, distance-from-peak, the gradient, and the `estimate` command are all absent. Note the issue's 'Related' numbers (#261/#263/#264) are vibey-gh-era issue numbers from before the monorepo absorption, not current vibey issue numbers.


<sub>Automated triage pass: every open issue re-read against the tree at `develop@f2467910`, each verdict then attacked by an independent verifier whose job was to refute it. Supersedes the 2026-09-15 triage, which was measured at 0.7.0.</sub>

**Status: PARTIAL · planning size: XL**

The estimator and preflight feasibility integration are present. The full 18-coordinate/six-material measurement model, cost integral, autonomous billing path, first-repair selection, and exact infeasible report still need completion and end-to-end validation.

Audited at `130afa0449fdcc65833f54ede596f0b4e45a145e`; this issue remains open. This comment supersedes older automated status notes.
